messages:
Ava: Anyone seen generator streams close early when I wrap requests with context.WithTimeout? sample app dies after ~200ms even though model should stream longer. Repro steps below.
Ava: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
res, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
// read loop ...
```
Ruben: hm could be auth refresh + handshake race, are you using token refresh middleware?
Priya: can you paste the raw logs around the close? we had a handshake goroutine that used background ctx before.
Ava: logs: 
```
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z generator: handshake initiated
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z auth: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z generator: stream started
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z read: got chunk size=128
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z read: stream closed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-10T15:02:10Z generator: handshake complete
```
Sam: sounds like the caller ctx triggers Done -> we close the transport -> but the auth refresh/handshake finishes slightly later and races with the close, resulting in an unexpected EOF.
Ruben: two possible approaches: 1) decouple internal handshake/auth from the caller ctx by using an internal ctx that only cancels on explicit Close(), or 2) implement a short grace period after ctx.Done before tearing down the read loop to let in-flight auth complete.
Priya: UX note — the quickstart uses context.WithTimeout for the whole generator call. we should document recommended patterns: prefer an overall request ctx for user-level timeouts but avoid very short WithTimeouts when using streaming; instead cancel with signal or a per-chunk deadline. I'll draft a sample.
Priya: suggested sample snippet to add to quickstart: 
```go
// prefer explicit cancel so internal handshake has time to finish
ctx := context.Background()
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
// when you want to stop streaming: cancel() then drain stream.Close()
```
Ava: workaround for now: removed WithTimeout and handle my own cancel on SIGINT; seems stable. filing issue.
ci-bot: Created issue #2387: "go-sdk stream: handshake cancels on parent ctx with auth refresh race" https://tracker.redwood.ai/issue/2387
Ruben: I'll pick this up — plan: make handshake use a child ctx with a short buffer (eg 5s) and add unit test that simulates token refresh delay + short caller deadline. also add quickstart note.
Priya: :thumbsup:
Ava: thanks — ping me when there's a patch, i can validate with the sample app and a scheduled auth-refresh test.
Sam: also let's add an integration test that runs the sample app with `context.WithTimeout(250*time.Millisecond)` to ensure we don't flake silently.
Ava: noted, thanks all.
